questions: In fully visible frames, does the component keep the normal upright/stable posture instead of lying on its side?
Does the component avoid tumbling, strong wobbling, rolling, or unstable rotation while moving?
Are the red cap and black pin side visible as opposite ends of the same component, with no clear reversed-orientation evidence?
Does the component move smoothly from LEFT to RIGHT across the video?
Does the component stay fully on the belt surface without overhanging, falling, or leaving the belt?

question_answers.evidence: The component is lying on its side with the metal pins pointing upwards and the red cap on the side face, rather than sitting upright on its base.
The component slides across the belt without tumbling or strong wobbling, maintaining its side-lying posture.
The red cap and the pin side are visible as distinct parts of the component, though the orientation is sideways.
The component moves smoothly from the left side of the frame to the right side.
The component remains fully on the green conveyor belt surface throughout the video.

parsed.reason: The component is lying on its side with pins pointing up and the red button on the side face, which violates the nominal upright/stable posture condition.

description: Push-button component with angle/alignment anomaly while moving on the conveyor belt.
